summary: The pre-market tone is defensive. The 2026-10-29 US close was weak in semis and memory, with the four-name semiconductor leaders basket down 2.4479% on average and Micron down 4.9795%; in the 2026-10-30 Asian session all 11 tracked A-shares closed lower, averaging a 4.4395% decline, led by memory and advanced packaging (603986.SH down 6.5908%). The composite risk score holds at 59.33 (caution), only 0.56 above the previous pre-market brief's 58.77, because the model is close-to-close and the pre-market server-maker rout is not yet in it. What did move is cross-asset confirmation: 6 of 8 production-scored signals are triggering, lifting that dimension to 75.00 and contributing 11.25 points on its own. Two things to watch: whether the Dell, HP and Super Micro pre-market declines carry into the open, and whether the 5.05% 10-year yield keeps pressuring long-duration tech.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation has climbed to 75.00: 6 of the 8 production-scored signals are triggering, the single largest contribution in the model at 11.25 points, lifting that dimension by 12.50 overnight from 62.50. The triggering set spans equities, the dollar, real rates, small-cap relative strength, copper and bitcoin, which reads as multi-point confirmation rather than a single noisy leg.

Rates carry most of the macro weight: the 10-year yield sits at 5.05% (prior 4.99%) and the 10-year real rate at 2.67% (prior 2.64%), the latter in the 98.24 percentile. The macro dimension reads 72.80 at a 20% weight, with the 10-year contributing 4.8395 points and the real rate 4.912. Rising yields alongside a dollar index of 121.3202 apply a double discount to richly valued growth stocks.

The AI hardware complex is de-rating systematically: the memory basket is down 5.0473%, enterprise software 3.5207% and AI infrastructure 3.2977%, with Micron off 4.9795% on the session. Memory is the weakest link, down 21.6699% over the month and sitting in the 5.0 percentile of its own year, which points to a trending drawdown rather than one-day sentiment.

Breadth is deteriorating, not repairing: the share of S&P 500 members above their 200-day average fell to 0.4516 (prior 0.4581), the new-low ratio rose to 0.1274 (prior 0.1154) and the new-high ratio is just 0.0318. Small-cap relative strength lags by 5.4583 percentage points accumulated over a 63-session window, which is a window measure and not a single-day figure.

Crypto is the night's independent risk source: bitcoin prints 77677.0, down 3.00289% over 24 hours, with ether down 3.3039% and SOL down 3.46672%. A Binance security incident is reported to be the largest crypto theft on record, so the news flow and the price action point the same way.

supporting_signals.claim: All 11 tracked A-shares closed lower on 2026-10-30, averaging a 4.4395% decline with a 4.9241% median, and this is a second consecutive down session rather than one-day noise. The worst are 603986.SH down 6.5908%, 300475.SZ down 6.5401% and 600584.SH down 5.5331%; over the week 10 of the 11 are negative.

Sector breadth is overwhelmingly negative: of 22 sector and theme rows, 4 are up and 18 down, with a 1.3699% mean decline and a 1.5555% median. The laggards are memory at 5.0473%, enterprise software at 3.5207%, AI infrastructure at 3.2977%, autonomous driving at 2.8958% and cloud at 2.8379%, uniformly the longest-duration growth verticals.

Credit is not following equities lower: the high-yield spread sits at 3.14% (prior 3.18%) and investment grade at 0.86% (prior 0.88%), both tighter, pulling the liquidity and credit dimension down from 66.37 to 62.84. This is a rate and duration shock, not a credit event.

contradicting_signals.claim: The options market does not share the equity tape's tension: VIX settled at 16.91 (prior 17.52) and the volatility dimension eased from 30.95 to 27.77, still the lowest of the six dimensions. If systemic risk were genuinely building, this is where it usually shows first.

Uptrend momentum is intact: on a one-week basis AMD is up 11.5154%, Micron 9.0813% and Broadcom 6.7318%, while the trend dimension actually rose from 43.60 to 45.06 and price still sits 5.6048% above its 200-day average. This still looks like a pullback within an uptrend rather than a confirmed reversal.

Two of the 4 positive rows out of 22 deserve scepticism: robotics at 2.1478% is all but identical to 6861.T alone at 2.1477%, meaning the last chain step collapsed onto a single Asian member, and consumer electronics at 1.0536% is just the average of the two Asian legs 1810.HK and 2317.TW. Scored on the US leg alone both baskets are negative, so the breadth of the sell-off is understated.

The near-flat score is itself counter-evidence: 59.33 versus 58.77 is only 0.56 higher, with 1.875 points from cross-asset and 0.146 from trend largely offset by 0.706 from liquidity and credit and 0.477 from volatility. The model has not yet absorbed the pre-market server-maker losses, so this reading lags.

what_changed_today: The score moved from 58.77 in the previous pre-market brief to 59.33, a rise of 0.56: cross-asset added 1.875 points and trend 0.146, offset by declines of 0.706 from liquidity and credit, 0.477 from volatility and 0.274 from macro.

The one cross-asset leg that flipped is equities: the S&P 500 went from up 0.3443% to down 0.382%, pushing the trigger count from 5 to 6 of 8 and lifting the cross-asset dimension from 62.50 to 75.00.
Breadth softened: the share above the 200-day average fell from 0.4581 to 0.4516 and the new-low ratio rose from 0.1154 to 0.1274, nudging the equity structure dimension from 60.84 to 61.41.
Crypto repriced lower: the 24-hour bitcoin move widened from down 1.55282% to down 3.00289%, coinciding with the largest security incident on record.
A-shares fell across the board for a second consecutive session, with 11 of 11 tracked names down and a 4.4395% average decline, a full round trip against the broad gains of the prior session.
watch_next: The US open: Dell is down 11.8%, HP 8% and Super Micro 6% in pre-market trading; watch whether those losses carry into the session and whether they spill over into the upstream server supply chain. Those figures are relayed via CLS over RSSHub, so they are second-hand aggregation.
Earnings today: Abbott, Chevron and Exxon are due around 12:00Z, with Chevron already at 5.28 actual versus 4.87 expected and Exxon at 4.23 versus 4.12, both beats.

Next week's macro calendar sets the direction: JOLTS job openings on 2026-11-03, the Employment Situation report on 2026-11-06 at high importance, and CPI on 2026-11-10 are the three gates for the rate path.
The US midterm election is on 2026-11-03 and the market is already pricing a change in congressional control, so policy expectations may move sector rotation ahead of fundamentals.

China liquidity and credit: the onshore credit bond market saw a concentrated sell-off with city-investment and bank perpetual yields moving sharply higher, even as the PBoC reiterated a moderately loose policy stance. If the pressure spreads, the liquidity and credit dimension will register it first.

bull_case.title: Bull case: yields retreat and the cross-asset gate loosens
points: If the 10-year yield retreats below 5.00% while the high-yield spread holds near 3.14%, the 6 triggered cross-asset legs could fall back to 4, taking that dimension from 75.00 back toward 50.00 and roughly 3.75 points off the total score.
A volatility reading of 27.77 and tightening credit spreads say the market is not in crisis mode, and one-week momentum (AMD up 11.5154%) still belongs to the bulls.

base_case.title: Base case: the score holds in caution while the index chops
points: The score oscillates between 55 and 62: rising rates and deteriorating breadth push it up, while calm volatility and credit markets hold it down.
The AI hardware complex keeps de-rating step by step, partly offset by non-duration laggards turning up, with industrial automation at 1.1815% and fintech at 1.5657%.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the server chain breaks and reaches the index
points: If the Dell and HP pre-market losses hold into the session and the Asian memory weakness (000660.KS down 7.0773%) transmits to US memory, the memory basket's 5.0473% decline could widen and breadth at 0.4516 would break further.
In that case cross-asset would hold at 6 or more triggered legs and, with rates refusing to fall, the score has room to push above 65.
